page.title: AI assistant
page.subtitle: Set up the in-app assistant and let external AI agents (Claude Code and others) work with lazyit over MCP. Off until an administrator turns it on.
page.loadError: The AI settings could not be loaded

enabled.title: The AI assistant is on
enabled.body: People with the “Use the AI assistant” permission now see the assistant in the top bar. Everyone else picks it up within a minute, or when they reload.

secretKey.title: The server has no AI_SECRET_KEY
secretKey.body: Provider API keys are stored encrypted with the AI_SECRET_KEY environment variable of the API. Until an operator sets it (a 32-byte key, for example from openssl rand -hex 32) and restarts the API, no key can be saved and only a keyless OpenAI-compatible server can be used. MCP does not need it.

serviceAccounts.body: Service accounts use the assistant without a person approving each change. Choose what each one may do — off, read-only or read and write, with an optional cap on writes — from its row menu in

descriptions.anthropic: Claude models, through the Anthropic API.
descriptions.openai: GPT models, through the OpenAI API.
descriptions.google: Gemini models, through the Google Gemini API.
descriptions.openai-compatible: Any server that speaks the OpenAI API — a self-hosted model on your network, a gateway, or another cloud. You give its base URL.

baseUrl.label: Base URL
baseUrl.description: The server's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, usually ending in /v1. No user name, password, query string or fragment — the key goes in the API key field.

problems.required: This provider needs a base URL.
problems.invalid: This is not a valid URL.
problems.scheme: The base URL must start with https:// (or http:// on a private network).
problems.credentials: Remove the user name or password from the URL — put the key in the API key field.
problems.queryFragment: Remove the query string (?…) or fragment (#…) from the URL.
problems.httpNeedsPrivate: A plain http:// address is only allowed for a server on your private network: turn on “Server on a private network” below.
problems.loopback: localhost is never reachable from the API container. Use the server's address on your network.

privateNetwork.label: Server on a private network
privateNetwork.description: Allow this one host on a private address (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x, or an internal name that resolves to one), plain http:// included. Loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused.

apiKey.label: {provider} API key
apiKey.placeholderKeep: A key is stored — leave blank to keep it
apiKey.placeholderOptional: Optional — leave blank if the server needs no key
apiKey.hintKeep: Type a new key only to replace the stored one.
apiKey.hintReplaced: Changing the provider or the base URL discards the stored key, so type the key for the new destination.
apiKey.hintOptional: A self-hosted server often needs no key.
apiKey.writeOnly: It is stored encrypted and never shown again — not even to administrators.

credentials.secretKeyMissing: This key cannot be saved yet: the API has no AI_SECRET_KEY. Ask the operator to set it and restart the API.

model.label: Model
model.description: The provider's model id. Pick a suggestion or type any id the provider accepts; the test below checks it.

effort.label: Reasoning effort
effort.description: Higher effort answers harder requests better, but is slower and uses more tokens.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.description: Between 0 and 2. Leave blank for the server's default.

wizard.title: Set up the AI assistant
wizard.subtitle: Choose a provider, give its key, pick a model and test it. Everything can be changed later.

provider.intro: The assistant sends what it reads to this provider to answer people. Pick the one your organization already trusts.

test.intro: Check that {provider} accepts the key, knows the model {model} and can call tools — the assistant cannot work without tool calling.
test.continueHint: The test must pass before you can continue.

disclosure.title: What leaves this server
disclosure.body: When someone uses the assistant, lazyit sends to {provider}:
disclosure.sent: the messages they type, the page they are on (its address and the record it shows), and the records the assistant reads to answer — assets, people, applications, access, stock and knowledge-base articles, limited to what that person may see;
disclosure.notSent: never vault secrets, passwords or the provider key itself, and nothing from pages the person did not ask about;
disclosure.retention: conversations are also stored on this server for the retention you choose below, and the provider's own data policy applies to what it receives.
disclosure.checkbox: I understand that this data is sent to {provider}, and I am allowed to send it there.

codes.PROVIDER_AUTH: The provider rejected the key. Check that it is correct, active, and allowed to use this model.
codes.PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT: The provider is rate-limiting this key. Wait a moment and test again.
codes.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE: The provider could not be reached or did not answer in time. Check the network path from the API server and try again.
codes.PROVIDER_BAD_REQUEST: The provider refused the request — usually an unknown model id or a setting this model does not support.
codes.PROVIDER_REFUSED: The provider refused to answer the test request.
codes.EGRESS_DENIED: lazyit refused to connect to this address: it is not a public host, or it is on your private network without “Server on a private network” turned on.
codes.TOOL_CALLING_UNSUPPORTED: The model answered but did not call a tool, so it cannot drive the assistant. Choose a model with tool calling.
codes.PROVIDER_LAYER_UNAVAILABLE: This build of lazyit cannot reach AI providers. Update the instance.

errors.network: The API could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.

gate.DISCLOSURE_REQUIRED: Acknowledge what leaves this server before turning the assistant on.
gate.PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED: Choose a provider and a model (and a base URL for an OpenAI-compatible server) before turning the assistant on.
gate.API_KEY_REQUIRED: This provider needs an API key before the assistant can be turned on.
gate.CONNECTION_TEST_FAILED: The connection test failed, so nothing was changed. Fix the problem below and try again.
gate.API_KEY_REQUIRED_DESTINATION_CHANGED: Changing the provider or the base URL discarded the stored key, so the assistant cannot be turned on without the key for the new destination. Type it and save again.

errors.secretKeyMissing: The API has no usable AI_SECRET_KEY, so the key cannot be stored and a keyed provider cannot be turned on. Ask the operator to set a 32-byte key (openssl rand -hex 32) and restart the API.
errors.shimMode: This instance runs with authentication disabled (AUTH_MODE=shim), where the AI assistant is never available.
errors.concurrentSave: Someone else changed the AI settings meanwhile. Reload the page and save again.

baseUrl.credentials: The base URL may not contain a user name or password — put the key in the API key field.
baseUrl.queryFragment: The base URL may not contain a query string or a fragment.
baseUrl.scheme: The base URL must be http:// or https://.
baseUrl.httpNeedsPrivate: A plain http:// base URL is only allowed for an OpenAI-compatible server on your private network, with “Server on a private network” turned on.
baseUrl.httpPublic: A plain http:// base URL must point at a private-network address, never a public one. Use https://.
baseUrl.loopback: A loopback address (localhost) is never allowed. Use the server's address on your network.
baseUrl.unreachable: This address range is never allowed (loopback, link-local, cloud metadata or reserved).
baseUrl.privateNeedsOption: This is a private-network address: choose the OpenAI-compatible provider and turn on “Server on a private network”.
baseUrl.invalid: The base URL is not a valid URL.

errors.privateNetworkProviderOnly: A private-network server is only allowed for the OpenAI-compatible provider.
errors.providerOptions: These extra settings are not supported by the selected provider.
errors.providerAndModelFirst: Choose a provider and a model before testing the connection.
errors.validation: Some values are out of range. Check the highlighted fields and try again.
errors.forbidden: You no longer have permission to manage the AI settings.
errors.notFound: This API does not have the AI settings. The instance may need an update.
errors.generic: The change could not be saved: {message}

connection.title: Provider & model
connection.description: Changing the provider, the base URL, the model or the key is tested again before it is saved; a failure changes nothing.

limits.title: Behaviour & limits
limits.description: How long conversations are kept, how much each person may use, and how the assistant behaves. Changes apply to new requests.

retentionDays.label: Keep conversations for
retentionDays.description: Older conversations are deleted automatically. The record of executed actions is kept regardless.
retentionDays.invalid: Enter a whole number of days between 7 and 3650.

approvalTtlMinutes.label: Approval cards expire after
approvalTtlMinutes.description: A proposed change that nobody approves in this time can no longer be approved.
approvalTtlMinutes.invalid: Enter a whole number of minutes, at least 1.

budget.label: Daily token budget per person
budget.description: Limit how many tokens one person or service account can use in any 24 hours. Off means no budget.

dailyTokenLimitPerPrincipal.label: Budget
dailyTokenLimitPerPrincipal.invalid: Enter a whole number of tokens, at least 1.

maxOutputTokens.label: Max reply length (tokens)
maxOutputTokens.invalid: Enter a whole number, at least 1.

maxStepsPerRun.label: Max steps per request
maxStepsPerRun.description: How many tool calls one request may chain.
maxStepsPerRun.invalid: Enter a whole number, at least 1.

contextTokenLimit.label: Conversation size limit (tokens)
contextTokenLimit.description: Past this, the person starts a new chat.
contextTokenLimit.invalid: Enter a whole number, at least 1.

instructions.label: Instructions for the assistant
instructions.placeholder: For example: our asset tags start with ACME-. Answer in Spanish unless asked otherwise.
instructions.description: Added to lazyit's own instructions for every conversation. They cannot widen what the assistant may do. {count} / {max} characters.

webSearch.title: Web search
webSearch.description: Let the chat assistant search the internet when lazyit's records and knowledge base don't have what it needs — for example, the documentation of a third-party product. The search runs at your AI provider.

switch.label: Allow the assistant to search the web
switch.description: Applies to conversations started after the change. Turning it off makes conversations that had it read-only.

availability.noProvider: Configure a provider first. Web search is available with Anthropic, OpenAI and Google Gemini 3 or later.
availability.providerUnsupported: The configured provider has no native web search, so the assistant can't search the web. It is available with Anthropic, OpenAI and Google Gemini 3 or later.
availability.modelUnsupported: The configured model can't search the web together with lazyit's tools. Choose Gemini 3 or later to use it.

disclosure.title: What leaves lazyit
disclosure.egress: The provider runs the search on its own servers: lazyit makes no request of its own. The search queries and the conversation context go to the provider, and its search may be billed separately.
disclosure.untrusted: Search results are content written by anyone on the internet. The assistant treats them as data, never as instructions, cites the pages it used, and a change it proposes in the same reply always needs your approval — even with auto-approve on.
disclosure.conversations: The chat only. Headless runs never search the web, because their changes run without anyone approving them.

maxUses.label: Searches per step
maxUses.description: The most searches the assistant may run in one model step, where the provider supports a limit (Anthropic).
maxUses.invalid: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.

mcp.title: External AI agents (MCP)
mcp.description: Let AI agents that run outside lazyit — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and others — read and change lazyit as the person who connects them, with that person's permissions. Independent of the assistant above: it works with no provider configured.

switch.label: Allow external AI agents
switch.description: People also need the “Connect external AI agents (MCP)” permission. Turning this off disconnects every client at once; their authorizations come back when you turn it on again.

oauth.title: This instance's public address is https://: clients sign in with OAuth
oauth.body: When a person adds lazyit to their client, the client opens a lazyit page in the browser where they review the access and approve it. Nothing to copy by hand, and each connection can be revoked from Account → AI & connected apps. (OAuth is available because the API's WEB_ORIGIN setting is an https:// address.)
oauth.internalCa: If your certificate comes from an internal certificate authority, Claude Code (and other Node.js clients) will not trust it until they are started with the authority's certificate:
oauth.cloud: Cloud connectors — claude.ai, Claude Desktop connectors and ChatGPT — connect from the provider's servers, not from the person's computer. They only work if this instance is reachable from the internet over HTTPS with a publicly trusted certificate.

personalToken.title: This instance has no https:// public address: clients use personal tokens
personalToken.body: Each person creates a personal MCP token in Account → AI & connected apps and gives it to their client (Claude Code asks for it when the lazyit plugin is enabled). Tokens expire and can be revoked there at any time.
personalToken.whyNoOauth: OAuth sign-in needs HTTPS and a fixed public address, so the API offers it only when its WEB_ORIGIN setting is an https:// address. A TLS proxy in front of lazyit is not enough on its own: set WEB_ORIGIN to the https:// address people use and restart the API to switch to OAuth.
personalToken.cloud: Cloud connectors (claude.ai, ChatGPT) cannot connect to this instance: they need a publicly reachable HTTPS address.

mode.detectedFromBrowser: The server's answer was not available, so this was guessed from the address in your browser. The real mode depends on the API's WEB_ORIGIN setting.
mode.loading: Checking how clients connect to this instance…

endpoint.label: MCP endpoint
endpoint.description: The address to give an MCP client that is set up by hand.
endpoint.pageFallback: The API has no pinned public address (WEB_ORIGIN), so this is the address of the page you are on. Clients on other machines may need the instance's LAN address instead.

install.description: Your connected apps and personal tokens are on Account → AI & connected apps; the install steps are below.

allowlist.title: Allowed clients
allowlist.description: Only these clients can connect. A client is recognized by its client-metadata URL or by the exact address it sends people back to after sign-in — never by the name it gives itself.

anyHttps.label: Accept any client with an https:// callback (on by default)
anyHttps.description: Any MCP client whose sign-in callback is an https:// address may ask a person for access, even if it is not listed here. Nothing is granted by this alone: the person still sees the consent page, which shows the client's callback host and warns that the client was not listed. Clients with a loopback or app-scheme callback (such as cursor://) still need an entry. Turn this off to accept only the clients listed below.

removed.title: Removed clients no longer in the built-in list
removed.description: You removed these built-in clients, but this version of lazyit no longer ships them. Restoring only clears the removal.

add.title: Add a client
add.label: Name
add.cimdHint: The https:// URL the client uses as its client id.
add.redirectHint: The exact address: https://…, http://127.0.0.1/… or http://localhost/… (any port), or an app scheme such as com.example.app:/callback or cursor://…
add.full: The list is full ({max} clients). Remove one to add another.

errors.cimdHttps: A client-metadata URL must start with https://.
errors.userinfo: The address may not contain a user name (…@…) — it could send people somewhere else.
errors.httpNotLoopback: Plain http:// is only allowed on 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1]. Use https:// for any other host.
errors.browserScheme: This kind of address can never be a callback.
errors.redirectInvalid: Use https://, a loopback http:// address, or an app scheme in reverse-domain form (com.example.app:) or a known editor scheme (cursor, vscode, vscode-insiders, windsurf).

allowlist.notSeeded: Pi, Windsurf and Zed are not in the built-in list because their identifiers could not be verified — add them below if your team uses them.

builtIn.title: Built-in clients
builtIn.description: The well-known clients lazyit allows out of the box. Remove one to stop it connecting (it is then only accepted if “any https:// client” admits it); restore it at any time.

danger.title: Turn off the AI assistant
danger.description: Hides the assistant for everyone. The configuration and the key are kept, so turning it back on is one step.

confirm.title: Turn off the AI assistant?
confirm.chat: the assistant disappears from the top bar and new requests are refused;
confirm.dormant: conversations are kept (and still deleted when their retention ends); changes waiting for approval cannot be approved while it is off;
confirm.kept: the provider, the model and the encrypted key are kept for when you turn it back on;
confirm.mcp: external AI agents (MCP) are not affected — they have their own switch.
